Those reach module-access-requests.ts:320 (GET) and :482 (decision), with POST / at :161 and GET /mine at :242. I checked that approval really unlocks the app. decideAccessRequest writes the grant with expiresAt:null under a FOR UPDATE row lock (module-access-requests.ts:375-418). canAccessModule allows any explicitly enabled grant before it checks tier (license-manager.ts:358-361). The nav resolver ranks the subscription row above tier (navigation-entitlements.ts:24-31). So an approved tier-locked request does unlock both the rail and the route gate. The member side is reachable: lockNotice marks 'disabled', 'industry' and 'tier' locks requestable for non-admins (navEntitlements.tsx:337-370), but launch-scope locks are not (:326-334). No CHECK constraint restricts organization_users.role (grep of migrations found none), so an 'owner' or 'business_admin' user sees the menu entry and gets a 403 from access-requests.ts:229-231 unless resolveMasterAdmin applies. That is a role-mapping defect, not a broken job. Traffic will stay low at launch, as they noted.

The toggle's role check reads req.user.role, which comes from the JWT (middleware/auth.ts:257). That claim is organization_users.role at login (routes/auth.ts:566, :776, :810), so a real org admin gets through. writeModuleGrant (module-grants.ts:93-140) upserts module_subscriptions. That is a real Part 11 §11.10(e) hole on an entitlement change. The client calls GET /api/billing/usage/limits, /invoices and /credits (UsageBilling.tsx:260,265,277), POST /portal (UsageBilling.tsx:295) and PUT /credits/auto-reload (UsageBilling.tsx:321). The only writer of api_usage_logs is recordApiUsage (server/services/usage-recorder.ts:100-118), which the AI gateway calls through recordApiUsageSafe (server/services/ai-gateway/gateway.ts:89,4183). All of their gaps hold. debitCredits (server/services/credit-ledger.ts:240) has no caller in server/. maybeAutoReload is called only at credit-ledger.ts:250. The only addCreditEntry caller is the platform-admin POST /credits/adjust (billing-dashboard.ts:916,934), so the balance never falls with use and a Stripe payment never adds credit. createPortalSession throws when the org has no stripe_customer_id (server/services/billing.ts:631-642), and billing.ts:166-168 turns that into a 500. The client shows that as an error toast, not a fake success (UsageBilling.tsx:302-313). requestsPerMinute appears in server/ only in billing-dashboard.ts, so nothing enforces the rate card. The card is the inline constant USAGE_RATE_LIMITS (UsageBilling.tsx:24-29). I found one thing they missed, and it sharpens gap (5). Weekly caps are enforced: enforceWeeklyLimit('requests') sits on /api/ana and /api/ana-ri (server/bootstrap/register-ai-routes.ts:24,28,34), and weekly_usage_limits is on the apply path (scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:798). A backend to set a cap also exists: PUT /api/billing/weekly-limits/:metric (billing-dashboard.ts:783). But no client file under client/src calls /weekly-limits, /weekly-overage or /seats. With no configured row the cap check does nothing (register-ai-routes.ts:20-22), so the governed weekly caps the copy promises cannot be set from anywhere in the UI. But deploy-migrate refuses to run on a database that install-fresh/drizzle push did not provision (scripts/db/deploy-migrate.mjs:20-28,97-102), so this is the normal provisioning path, not a missing table. Duplicate confirmed: 'Usage & limits' and 'Billing' are two account-menu entries (Shell.tsx:211-212) that open the same component (surfaceViews.ts:581-582). Verdict: real data and real actions, but the money and credit loop is broken, so real-partial.

items.label: Set up a workspace (account menu) / "Set up your workspace" wizard
items.does: A signed-in admin goes through 7 steps: organization, pricing model, plan, invites, modules, agency accounts, review. On Activate the wizard renames the current org through a governed, audited PATCH and sets its industry profile. It creates one member invitation per email entered, then either provisions the free tier in the database, starts a Stripe checkout for a paid tier, or (enterprise) files a licence_requests row for the sales team. The completion screen reports honestly what each step did and did not do.

check.reason: Confirmed real-partial. I checked every write the assessor named and each reaches a mounted route: PATCH /api/organizations/:id/profile (organizations-routes.ts:293, requireOrgAdmin, reason required by the schema at :286); /api/mdx/industry-profile (mdx-industry-context.ts:132, mounted at register-inline-routes.ts:1213); POST /api/tenant-users (tenant-users.ts:378, mounted at register-tenant-routes.ts:57, called from startup/routes.ts:196); /api/billing (register-inline-routes.ts:202). Stripe is off in production: getStripe throws without STRIPE_SECRET_KEY (server/services/billing.ts:54-58; the assessor's billing.ts:56-58 means this services file, not routes/billing.ts). STRIPE appears in no file under terraform/; it appears only in docker-compose.beta.yml:155. So /checkout (routes/billing.ts:97) and paid /dtc-checkout (:217) return 500, and only the free tier and the enterprise licence request finish. Both billing routes carry only authenticateToken, and the 'Set up a workspace' menu entry has no gate (Shell.tsx:215). The step-5 module list is fixture text (Onboarding.tsx:358-385, 1094-1113). I found three defects the assessor missed. (1) The wizard writes a fixed reason on its audited Part 11 writes ('Organization name set during workspace activation.' at Onboarding.tsx:441 and 'Organization industry set...' at :462). The user never typed it, which breaks the repo's own rule at onboarding-proposals.ts:218 ('the human's own words — never synthesized on their behalf'). (2) The price shown can differ from the price charged. The wizard prices per-user plans by the client-side archetype family (Onboarding.tsx:318-326, from organization_industry_profiles). The server prices by organizations.industry_mode, defaulting to 'virtual_biotech', which is aliased to pharma (billing.ts:366-369, :326). The wizard never writes industry_mode: the profile PATCH body holds only name and reason (Onboarding.tsx:439-442). So a medtech org could see $349 per user and be charged $459 per user once Stripe is wired. (3) An invite counts as 'created' on any 2xx (Onboarding.tsx:490). The server returns 201 even when the activation email failed (tenant-users.ts:526-537, delivery:'failed'), and the wizard does not show that failure. The fixture prices match the server's cent values (onboarding-data.ts:22-55 vs billing.ts:104-230), so the price list itself has not drifted. The duplication with Setup, AdminAccess and Licensing stands.

items.does: A user uploads one PDF, Word or text file. The server virus-scans it, extracts the text, and asks the AI gateway for 10 target fields. It keeps only values whose quoted excerpt is verified to occur in the document. The human reviews and edits each value next to its provenance, enters a reason, and clicks Apply. An org admin can then write only organization name, client type and industry mode to the organizations row, with an audit entry. Program and contact values (7 of the 10 fields) are shown, then reported as 'not applied'.

items.label: Identity console (Enterprise identity: SSO / SCIM)

They can list SCIM IP allowlist rules and add new ones, and copy four SAML endpoint URLs. A customer org admin, who is linked here from Setup, sees only 'Platform administrator required'. SAML providers cannot be configured from this screen.

GET /api/part11/audit-trail/chain-integrity recomputes record_hash from row content (part11-compliance.ts:903-940), but its timestamp serialization can never equal the trigger's.
- The trigger hashes COALESCE(NEW.timestamp::text,'') (db/migrations/20260222_audit_events_hash_chain.sql, record_hash block). That file is on the apply path at scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:1590.
- audit_events.timestamp is `timestamp` without time zone (shared/schema.ts ~:10410, timestamp('timestamp').defaultNow(); migrations/0000_sweet_joseph.sql:139+). Its ::text is 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff', with no zone suffix and microsecond precision.
- The route's primary form is toISOString().replace('T',' ').replace('Z','+00'), which always carries '+00' and exactly 3 ms digits.
- Its fallback is String(row.timestamp), a JS Date string, because no setTypeParser exists anywhere under server/ (grep: none).
- I ran both forms in node (TZ=UTC) against '2026-10-07 12:34:56.123456'. Neither matched. A whole-second value cannot match either ('...:56' vs '...:56.000+00').
- Result: every trigger-hashed row lands in brokenLinks (:930-938). chainStatus becomes 'broken' and integrityValid false, because 'broken' outranks 'unverifiable' (:946-953).

- So any org written to since the trigger deployed on 2026-09-10 sees 'broken · Integrity broken · N broken links' on its Part 11 console: a false tamper alarm.
- The repo itself says content re-derivation is unsound for this table. chainIntegrityMonitor.ts:12-15 reads: 'does NOT re-derive record_hash … no single canonical record_hash serialization'; the signed export is linkage-only for the same reason.
